minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 20, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:02 p.m., on October 20, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 15, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:02
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

City Council Minutes  1  October 20, 2014
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Volunteer Dick Muth for his 15 years of service with the Meals on Wheels
  Program

  Mayor Kelley presented a certificate of appreciation to Dick Muth.

P2. Recognize City Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of appreciation to Darlene Chadick and Donna Rankin
  for volunteer hours with the Mission Viejo Library, and Dan Heller for volunteer hours with
  Animal Services.

P3. 20th Anniversary Celebration of the Mission Viejo Animal Services Center on
  November 1, 2014

  The City Council received the presentation from Sharon Cody.

P4. Featured Business of the Month - Jump ’n Jammin

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Eric and Nancy Barnes.

P5. Rate Study Presentation by Moulton Niguel Water District

  The City Council received the presentation from Joone Lopez and Matt Collings of Moulton
  Niguel Water District.

P6. PACE Programs (Property Assessed Clean Energy)

  The City Council received presentations from Dustin Reilich from Hero Program, Erik
  Caldwell from FigTree Company and Jeremy Hutman from CaliforniaFirst.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Michael Beck, Vice President of Operations, Mission Hospital: provided an update on the closure
of operating rooms for elective surgeries last week after three post-surgery infections occurred at
the hospital in May and June this year. Mr. Beck noted that emergency and trauma services have
not been impacted while the hospital reviews all of its practices and systems to assure that there is
not a reoccurrence of infections. Mr. Beck concluded with information on the institution of
policies and procedures relative to Ebola so that the hospital is prepared to manage it, if necessary.

City Council Minutes  2  October 20, 2014
 Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he is trying to implement meaningful changes to benefit
the residents of Mission Viejo. He said that he is hopeful for the future with a newly reconstituted
City Council and that the two biggest citizen concerns are traffic and police services. Mr.
Wontrobski offered suggestions for tackling these issues.

Anna Warner, M.V.: provided an update on the status of the project at her home where there is
water damage, mold and lack of a vent on the drain line. She stated that she was defrauded when
she purchased the home and she asked why after-the-fact building permits are given so easily and
she asked that no building permits be issued unless the project meets state code.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4 and 6 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 6, 2014, as presented.

5.  Conflict of Interest Code

  Adopted Resolution 14-49 Amending the City of Mission Viejo Conflict of Interest Code.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for August 2014

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  October 20, 2014
 8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2014

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for August 2014

  Received and filed.

10. Biennial City Commission Member Term Expiration

  (1) Directed the City Clerk to post the Notice of City Commission Vacancies, (2) set
  application deadline for December 12, 2014, and (3) scheduled appointment of commission
  members for January 5, 2015.

11. Orange County Transportation Authority 2015 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects: Measure M2 Regional Capacity Program

  Adopted Resolution 14-50 Approving the Submittal of a Candidate City of Mission Viejo
  Transportation Project to the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) for Funding
  Consideration Under the OCTA Measure M2 Comprehensive Transportation Funding
  Program for Regional Capacity Projects.

NEW BUSINESS

12. Special Olympics World Games 2015 - Host Town Program

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  Joseph Gorin, Special Olympics athlete, Laguna Niguel: discussed how the Special Olympics
  have made a significant difference in his life and he expressed support for the City of Mission
  Viejo to become a host town for the 2015 Special Olympics.

  The following presented a written comment in favor of the recommended action: Helen
  Workun, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to direct staff to
  commit to becoming a host town for the Special Olympics World Games in 2015.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  4  October 20, 2014
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated September 26, 2014 in the Amount of $3,035,927.52

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about checks written for pool maintenance, street
  resurfacing services, a program at the Discovery Science Center, a Lego camp conducted by
  the Friends of the Arts, and holiday lighting costs.

  Staff answered questions where possible and agreed to get back to the Council where further
  information was needed.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register Dated October 3, 2014 in the Amount of $699,712.24

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about the change in check numbers on the register.

  Director of Administrative Services replied that the new numbers are attributed to the
  implementation of the new accounting software.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2014

  Council Member Schlicht asked about the cash disbursements for CalPERS HCH.

City Council Minutes  5  October 20, 2014
   Director Dyas responded with an explanation of the different PERS payments that are
  processed during payroll.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:31 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:40
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

13. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the Firefighters Union has contributed $13,000 to a PAC to
  support various Mission Viejo City Council candidates in their election. He noted that the union
  contract is coming up for approval and his goal is to have a COIN review by both the public and
  the Council Members prior to the OCFA Board approving the contract.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

14. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

15. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

16. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

17. Orange County Vector Control District

City Council Minutes  6  October 20, 2014
   Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager Wilberg provided an update with regards to the ambulance services RFP. He
reminded the Council that the County took over the process and the matter is scheduled to go to
the Board of Supervisors on October 28 for a decision. The County is recommending that Doctor's
Ambulance continue to be the provider for Mission Viejo. He noted that he forwarded a copy of
a protest letter submitted by Doctor's which expressed concern that during the course of the
evaluation process, the criteria changed. Several cities are going to be submitting letters to the
Board of Supervisors expressing similar concerns with the process and although it could have an
impact on how things proceed, Mr. Wilberg noted that at this point it looks like Doctor's will
continue to provide service to the residents of Mission Viejo.

18. Resolution Making Findings Related to Approval of the Second Amendment to OCFA
  Joint Powers Authority Agreement - Equity

  City Attorney Curley presented the staff report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: asked why a copy of the appeal was not included with the staff
  report and he noted that the superior court judge stated that payments to the City of Irvine
  were illegal and a gift of public funds. He asked for the City Attorney's written opinion that
  rejects the judge's decision and questioned staff's position that member cities don't have any
  liability if OCFA goes bankrupt.

  Council Member Ury vacated the dais for a few minutes and returned at 8:23 p.m.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to adopt
  Resolution 14-51 Making Findings Related to Approval of the Second Amendment to the
  Amended Orange County Fire Authority Joint Powers Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Reardon
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Ury

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

City Council Minutes  7  October 20, 2014
 Council Member Reardon

Referring to the Mission Viejo Means Business newsletter, Council Member Reardon noted that
the Chamber is hosting a ribbon cutting for a new business called Boxfli on October 23 at 4:30
p.m. She also announced that the City is hosting two business workshops in October beginning
with a cyber-security program on October 23 from 9:00 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. The workshop is free
and more information is available by calling (714) 564-7200. The next program, Getting Started
with Facebook Marketing, takes place on October 30 for a cost of $139 and those interested can
register online. Council Member Reardon announced that she will be out of town so she cannot
join in the celebration of the 20th anniversary of the animal shelter but she recognized that the
shelter does a great job and continues to provide excellent service to the community. Council
Member Reardon shared that the Sheriff’s department has been doing some really good things
around prescription drug abuse including a seminar called Prescription for Life which will be
coming to Mission Viejo soon. The city has also launched a new webpage dedicated to drug abuse
at www.cityofmissionviejo.org/drugfree. The four-part video series, An Invisible Line, can be
found on the page as well as a host of other resources and links. Council Member Reardon
discussed the Solace program which holds meetings at the community center and was formed to
help parents who have either lost a child or are dealing with the addiction nightmare. She stated
that she has met a lot of very vocal and supportive residents and she thanked the City manager and
her colleagues for providing the support to deal with drug abuse issues.

Council Member Schlicht

Reading from a prepared statement, Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with
expenditures for the 2013 ITF Wheelchair Masters tournament and the Sierra Recreation Center
playground. She accused staff of allowing a Council Member to rig the bid for street sweeping
services and the city manager of offering the Nadadores a sweetheart deal for use of the Marguerite
swim complex. She noted that the Council majority passed items that she pulled from the Consent
Calendar without discussion when she was absent at the September 15, 2014 meeting. She stated
that this action showed lack of consideration towards her and contempt towards open and
transparent government. Council Member Schlicht discussed the nature of the questions she had
on those items she had removed from the Consent Calendar and she presented a copy of her
statement to the City Clerk for the public record. Council Member Schlicht referred to a
communication she received from the FPPC opining that the City was not in violation of the
Political Reform Act by allowing Council Member Reardon’s videos to remain on YouTube during
election season and suggesting that she contact the DA’s office regarding misuse of public
funds. She asked the City Attorney whether or not he has concluded his investigation into that
matter. City Attorney Curley stated that he does not give opinions in open meetings but he thinks
it is unlikely that the DA would address the matter. Council Member Schlicht concluded her
comments with a quote from Proverbs 15:22: “Without counsel, plans go awry but in a multitude
of counselors they are established.”

City Council Minutes  8  October 20, 2014
 Council Member Ury

20.  Permit Fee Waiver Program for Water Conservation Improvements

  Council Member Ury presented his report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve
  a permit fee waiver program for water conservation improvements and directed staff to
  return with the necessary budget amendment to cover City costs within 90 days of actual
  implementation.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Ury discussed his attendance at the Walk Against Drugs and he commended the
young man who gave the key note speech. He noted that it was a very inspirational story and an
all-around great event.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness announced that this year’s Camp Out was great and it was bigger than
ever with 600 attendees. He thanked Mark Nix, Barb Cassidy and Ashley Blair for a terrific job
taking care of everyone. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness discussed his encounter with a couple who
were there to camp with their grandkids and a single mom who had a broken foot and he helped
her put up her tent. He noted that it was a perfect event and he reiterated his thanks to staff and to
the Mission Viejo Activities Committee.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley commended the Marine Adoption Committee and City staff for another very
successful golf tournament last Friday. It is projected that there will be quite a bit of money raised
for the City's adopted Marine battalion which will provide family support, help with marine
attendance at the annual marine ball and many practical needs for the families. She noted that she
very much appreciates the work of the Adoption Committee and the staff members who are so
dedicated to this annual event. Mayor Kelley also commended Tammy Descoteaux and Chief
NewMyer for the successful Walk Against Drugs. Participants heard a strong message from the
inspirational speaker and it was another very successful event. Mayor Kelley noted that she has
been speaking with Chief NewMyer about bringing back a community program called "Is Your
Teen at Risk?" which is basically a combination of public safety and community resources coming
together to provide information for parents. She encouraged residents to watch for further details
on the program in the near future. Mayor Kelly discussed the Disaster Preparedness Expo and
thanked Supervisor Pat Bates for bringing that event to the City about 5 years ago. The expo
City Council Minutes  9  October 20, 2014
 showcases information on how to be prepared, what an earthquake kit should look like, and
provides very timely information that everyone should have and act on. Mayor Kelley reminded
residents that Hometown Halloween will be held on Saturday, October 25 at the Community
Center and Oso Viejo Park from 4:00 to 8:00 p.m. and she concluded her comments by reading a
note from a resident to the employees of Mission Viejo, thanking them for making the city such a
wonderful place to live.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:56 p.m. with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, November 3, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 3, 2014

City Council Minutes  10  October 20, 2014
